title: THE ONE authoritative readiness decision (box-status.operational_readiness)
description: SECTION 7. Source: src/box/operationalReadiness.ts buildOperationalReadiness(), driven by src/box/engine.ts operationalReadiness(). The SINGLE verdict a client must render instead of recombining raw facts. Readiness was previously answered in three disagreeing places: box-status (raw transports), GET /api/runtime/status (live_entry.blocked, computed from env/DB/token facts that included NEITHER transport lifecycle), and the frontend (its own matrix from market-data readiness plus one reconcile flag). Both HTTP surfaces are now projections of THIS decision. Entry and exposure permissions come from the SAME streamHealthPolicy combinedPermissions table the live-entry checkpoint enforces. NO SECRETS: states, counts, ages, booleans, bounded sentences and a MASKED account reference only — never a token, a passcode or a full account id. It promises nothing about fills, four-leg atomicity or maximum loss; entry.permitted means only that every observable precondition is currently satisfied.

decision_generation.description: Monotonic per-decision counter, SCOPED TO instance.instance_id. A response carrying a LOWER value than one already rendered FROM THE SAME INSTANCE is stale and must be IGNORED. It is PROCESS-LOCAL and resets to 0 on restart, so it must NOT be compared across instances: doing so left a browser holding generation 5000 rejecting a restarted backend's generation 1 indefinitely. Use instance.boot_ordinal to order across a restart.

instance.description: WHICH backend process decided this, and where it sits in the restart order. Source: src/box/backendInstance.ts. A decision is ordered by the pair (boot_ordinal, decision_generation) compared lexicographically; instance_id only tells a client whether it is still the same process. The shared ordering rule is orderReadinessDecision() in that module, which the frontend vendors rather than reimplementing — two implementations of an ordering protocol is how the two sides come to disagree about which verdict is current.

instance_id.description: Identifies THIS process. Random and non-secret. Carries NO ordering: a random value cannot express 'newer', so a client must never treat an unfamiliar id as automatically newer. Null only for a backend predating this contract, which is then unorderable.

boot_ordinal.description: Restart-durable, strictly increasing ordinal for this boot, minted atomically by PostgreSQL (migration 009_backend_instance_epoch.sql). NOT a clock: an NTP step, a VM snapshot restore or a skewed container clock must not be able to make an older instance look newer. NULL means the backend could not establish it because its authoritative store was unreachable at boot; the decision is then UNORDERABLE and a client MUST NOT let it overwrite an ordered decision and MUST disable new entry. The server independently refuses entry in that state too (blocker code instance_epoch_unknown), so safety does not depend on the client noticing.

started_at.description: Wall-clock ms this process started. AUDIT ONLY — never used for ordering, because a wall clock cannot order instances correctly.

decision_version.description: The version of this decision shape. A client that does not recognise it must degrade to 'unknown', never to a green light.

decided_at.description: Wall-clock ms at which the decision was evaluated. With decision_generation this is how a client tells current from stale.

account_masked.description: MASKED account reference, e.g. "AB••34". Never the raw id. Null when no account is bound.

account_present.description: Whether an account is bound at all — deliberately distinct from 'the id is hidden'.

state.description: The ACTUAL market-data lifecycle from the driven MarketDataStateMachine — not a feed_healthy boolean.

generation.description: Feed/session generation. Advances on every (re)authentication; a book observed under a superseded socket is not evidence for the new one.

usable_for_entry.description: True ONLY in READY: fresh usable depth per traded instrument in the current generation.

source.description: WHERE the quotes come from. broker_websocket is the only value that may be presented as executable streaming depth, and even then only when ticks_observed is true. rest_snapshot_fallback is the documented indicative/last-close REST view and is NOT equivalent: it must be labelled as fallback, never as executable depth. none means neither is available.

socket_connected.description: RAW TRANSPORT FACT: is the quote socket open right now. Deliberately separate from state/usable_for_entry, because an open socket that has delivered no book is connected and NOT usable — a distinction a single status field cannot express, and whose absence let an open socket be read as readiness.

authenticated.description: RAW TRANSPORT FACT: the broker session behind the feed reports itself authenticated. Not readiness.

subscriptions_requested.description: Whether a non-empty subscription set has been REQUESTED for the current generation. Deliberately not 'confirmed': Zerodha sends no subscription acknowledgement, so confirmation would be an assumption. Confirmation is evidenced by depth actually arriving (see depth_observations).

usable_books.description: Instruments holding a currently usable executable book (two-sided depth in the current generation).

ticks_observed.description: Whether ANY frame has been received in the current generation. THIS is the field that licenses a 'real broker WebSocket quotes' claim in the UI. An open socket alone must never produce it.

heartbeats_observed.description: Transport keep-alives seen. Proves the socket is alive and proves NOTHING about any book's freshness — a heartbeat can never warm an instrument or refresh a depth timestamp.

depth_observations.description: Usable two-sided book observations in the current generation. frames_observed > 0 with depth_observations === 0 is a real, nameable state: the socket is alive but delivering no executable depth.

lifecycle.description: The AUTHORITATIVE order-stream lifecycle the entry gate scored. Defect (a) was that this could be DEGRADED while the published health said LIVE.

published_state.description: The same fact as published in order_stream.brokers[].health.state, DERIVED from the lifecycle above so the two cannot disagree.

wiring.description: not_applicable_paper: this deployment SIMULATES execution, so no order is sent to the broker and the broker has no order to report on. A paper process constructs no order-stream consumer BY DESIGN (building one implies a live order manager). This is the expected configuration, NOT a fault, and must never render as not_wired — whose meaning is 'this should be running and is not'.

fill_observation.description: The mechanism ACTUALLY responsible for observing a fill right now.

mechanism.description: simulated_paper_fills: fills are produced by the LOCAL execution simulator against real streamed quotes. A broker cannot emit an order-update event for an order it never received, so reporting paper fills as rest_polling_only was not a conservative understatement but false — it implied a broker round trip and a confirmation that do not exist.

evidence.description: How old the evidence behind this decision is. NULL means NEVER OBSERVED — it must never render as a fresh 0. The four time facts are kept distinct: a heartbeat is not a depth update.

market_data_last_frame_at.description: WALL-CLOCK (epoch ms) stamp of the last frame, for audit and display only. NEVER the basis of an age — see market_data_age_clock.

market_data_last_depth_at.description: WALL-CLOCK (epoch ms) stamp of the last usable depth observation, for audit and display only.

market_data_age_clock.description: Which clock produced the market-data ages above, published so a reader can VERIFY the domains were not mixed rather than trust that they were not. The defect this documents: the engine stamped frame/depth/heartbeat times with executionClock.mono() but the builder subtracted executionClock.wall() as `now`, yielding ages of ~1.7e12 ms (about 55 years). Always positive, so the zero floor could not reveal it, and a dashboard could only render it as garbage or as 'never observed' — which is exactly the reported 'last frame never observed' while ticks were arriving normally.

paper_execution.description: HOW EXECUTION IS ACTUALLY PERFORMED, published separately from any broker order stream and present in EVERY payload so a reader never has to decide whether an order-stream field applies. When simulated is true, fills come from the local simulator and no broker confirmation exists or is possible — a normal, healthy state, not a degraded one.

simulated.description: True in every paper mode. The process contains no object capable of placing a real order.

profile.description: The paper profile in force (e.g. paper_latency), or null under live.

using_streamed_quotes.description: Whether the simulator is currently pricing against REAL streamed depth. True only when depth has actually been observed in the current generation — never inferred from an open socket.

detail.description: Plain language, safe to display verbatim. Says 'Real broker WebSocket quotes · simulated execution' ONLY when tick evidence supports it, and says so explicitly when it does not.

pending.description: True while a REST gap repair is owed. A gap is NEVER assumed empty; missing events are not zero fills.

entry.description: NEW ENTRY: the single verdict, plus every reason it was refused. A client MUST NOT show a permitted state when this is false.

exposure_management.description: REDUCING exposure, computed from reduction-scoped facts ONLY. THE INVARIANT: an entry-scoped restriction (stopped scanner, entry disabled, spent session budget, entry capital cap, one-active-underlying, unavailable reservations, entry-only market-data requirements, an unrelated symbol's stale book) can NEVER appear here and can never independently block a reduction. Reduction keeps its own genuine requirements — an expired session or an unpriceable book still refuses it, and says so.

limitations.description: What reduction cannot promise even when permitted. Always non-empty: permission is not a fill, four-leg atomicity is unavailable, and an unpriceable leg cannot be reduced on a limit price.
